title: Odile and the Letter
premise: Retired detective Tamsin Zhou receives a confession letter for a drowning ruled accidental—postmarked the day after the victim's funeral. The letter names a witness, Mara Voss, whom every record insists died years ago in the same coastal town where Tamsin once failed to save a girl. As Tamsin investigates against police pressure and her own grief, she discovers the confession was written by a dying woman protecting her son, and that Mara faked her death to escape him. In the end, Tamsin finds Mara alive at the tide line, chooses justice outside the law by withholding evidence that would destroy an innocent life, and finally allows herself to belong—to the town, and to the bookshop she almost sold.
about_author: Elodie Reyes is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipwreck records along the northern coast before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about small towns that keep their dead close and their truths closer.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Sorting through her failing bookshop's mail, Tamsin finds a confession letter describing a murder the coroner called an accident—postmarked the day after the funeral. The handwriting trembles; the details are precise. When she drives to the coastal house named inside, she finds it freshly painted over old bloodstains. Emotional beat: dread reawakening instincts she buried with her badge.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Drowned Twice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Records say witness Mara Voss died seven years ago—a body, a burial, a headstone Tamsin herself once visited. Yet the letter describes conversations that continued long after. Digging into parish archives and a fisherman's loose tongue, Tamsin learns the coffin was sealed early and the family paid for silence. Emotional beat: obsession tightening as her past failure entwines with this case.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, climax. Confronting the confessor's son on the storm-battered pier, Tamsin realizes he killed to protect his mother's secret—and that Mara has been hiding in the lighthouse keeper's cottage all along. A violent struggle nearly takes Tamsin into the sea; the tide gives up what it took when the victim's missing locket washes ashore between them. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into fierce clarity about what justice actually requires.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, resolution. With the son arrested on unrelated charges and the mother's confession burning in her grate, Tamsin meets Mara at dawn on the tideline. Two women who chose invisibility recognize each other. Tamsin lets the truth stay buried, keeps the bookshop off the market, and pins a new notice in the window: open. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace—the choice to be seen.
